name: colMads
title: Standard deviation estimates for each row (column) in a matrix

origin.description: Standard deviation estimates for each row (column) in a matrix.
origin.usage:
colMads(x, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, center = NULL, constant = 1.4826,
  na.rm = FALSE, dim. = dim(x), ..., useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An NxK matrix or, if dim. is specified, an N * K vector.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of rows to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of columns to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: center
arguments.text: The center, defaults to the column medians for the MAD estimators. A scalar is defunct unless it already has one value per column.

arguments.name: constant
arguments.text: A scale factor. See stats::mad for details. The default is 1.4826.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

arguments.name: dim.
arguments.text: An integer vector of length two specifying the dimension of x, also when not a matrix. The argument is named with a period so it does not clash with dim.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

origin.details: Same estimator as rowMads, applied down each column. The installed function calls the row routine with byrow FALSE. With center set, the column centers are subtracted by t_tx_OP_y, which casts integers to double before subtracting, and the result is constant times colMedians of the absolute values.
origin.value: A numeric vector of length K, one median absolute deviation per selected column.

translation.description: Standard deviation estimates for each column in a matrix.
translation.usage:
colMads(x, rows=None, cols=None, center=None, constant=1.4826, na_rm=False,
  dim=None, use_names=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A 2-d array whose axis 0 is rows and axis 1 is columns, matching the printed R matrix. A 1-d vector is accepted when dim is set; it is filled column-major, as R stores a matrix. Integer values use the 32-bit path. Floating values are computed as float64. Logical input is rejected.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based row subscripts. None selects every row. The values of a column are taken in this order.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: 1-based column subscripts. None selects every column. Zeros are dropped, negatives exclude, and logical values are recycled.

arguments.name: center
arguments.text: One center per column. None uses each column's own median. A single number is an error unless the matrix has one column. Integer centers are subtracted in double precision, matching t_tx_OP_y, so a difference past the 32-bit range is kept.

arguments.name: constant
arguments.text: Scale factor, default 1.4826, the same default as stats::mad. A one-value column returns 0 without using this factor.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, missing values are excluded. This is na.rm. False turns a missing value into R's NA.

arguments.name: dim
arguments.text: Two integers giving the number of rows and columns. This is dim. in R. None uses the shape of a 2-d x. A 1-d x is filled in column-major order.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: Accepted for the R argument useNames. It must be TRUE or FALSE. The result is a plain array, with no names attached.

translation.details: The scan lives in the Rust crate rowmads, ported from matrixStats src/rowMads.c with byrow FALSE and hasNA TRUE. It is the column form of rowMads, including the constant 1.4826 and the same missing-value and one-observation rules. When center is set, subtraction is done in float64 and the median of the absolute deviations is multiplied by constant.
translation.value: A float64 vector of length K, one median absolute deviation per selected column.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.rowmads import colMads

x = np.arange(1, 13).reshape((4, 3), order="F")
colMads(x)
